stops.title: Gezicht op huizen in Delft ('The Little Street')
stops.story_quote: Vermeer first painted the door to the house closed, then chose to open it, allowing a shaft of light
specifics_traced: underpainting shows the door originally closed (documented technical finding)
included property of his aunt van der Minne (documented)

stops.title: De bedreigde zwaan (The Threatened Swan)
stops.story_quote: The decision by the Nationale Kunst-Galerij's founders to select this as their inaugural purchase set the tone
specifics_traced: Jan Asselijn, c.1650, oil on canvas, 144x171cm (documented)
first purchase of the Nationale Kunst-Galerij, forerunner of the Rijksmuseum (confirmed)
later read as political allegory re: Johan de Witt (confirmed)

stops.title: Het melkmeisje (The Milkmaid)
stops.story_quote: By making The Milkmaid a centerpiece of the exhibition, Dibbits underscored how this modest canvas continues to shape the museum's view
specifics_traced: Taco Dibbits is the Rijksmuseum's real director (plausible, true person) though the specific exhibition claim is thin

fabrications.claim: Dibbits 'made The Milkmaid a centerpiece of the exhibition' as a specific documented act
fabrications.why: vague, unsourced curatorial claim attached to a real name without a traceable event

stops.title: De grote golf bij Kanagawa (The Great Wave)
stops.story_quote: Its composition is said to have inspired works like Debussy's La Mer and Rilke's Der Berg
specifics_traced: Hokusai, c.1831, Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (documented)
woodblock printing process with carver/printer collaboration (documented)

fabrications.claim: 'inspired works like Debussy's La Mer and Rilke's Der Berg'
fabrications.why: the Great Wave's influence on Debussy is a widely repeated but disputed/unverified claim, and the Rilke poem connection is not established — stated as settled fact

stops.title: A Militiaman Holding a Berkemeyer ('Merry Drinker')
stops.story_quote: Hals, painting in the late 1620s, chose to present the sitter not in stiff formality but alive in the company of others
specifics_traced: Frans Hals, c.1628-1630, oil on canvas 81x66.5cm (documented)

defects: Stray sentence about a militiaman opens Stop 1 before the Orientation (misplaced from Stop 6)
Stop 5 contains a truncated sentence ('This work w.')
Stop 4 has no concrete body specifics, only a Dibbits name-drop
Two unverifiable embellishments (Dibbits exhibition claim, Debussy/Rilke influence) stated as fact
one_line_verdict: Real, well-documented works and strong story content at 3/6 stops; two unverifiable 'inspired later artists' flourishes.
